name: Ottoman Capture of Thessaloniki
summary: Sultan Murad II captures Thessaloniki (then under Venetian administration since 1423) on March 29, 1430 after a brief siege. The Venetians had purchased the city from the Byzantine Despot to defend it; they fail. Murad's forces sack the city for three days; many inhabitants are enslaved, including reportedly the entire population of some quarters. The city's churches are converted to mosques. Thessaloniki is the second city of Byzantium and its loss signals the complete encirclement of Constantinople.

_quarry.structural_significance: Completes Ottoman encirclement of Constantinople; demonstrates that Venice cannot hold Byzantine cities against determined Ottoman siege; the population enslavement causes a Greek diaspora to Italy, accelerating Renaissance Hellenism; precedes the final fall of Constantinople by 23 years
